articles.title: Hawaii and Florida top list of best US beaches for 2026, according to ‘Dr. Beach’
articles.summary: The list of the top 10 beaches in the United States is dominated by Hawaii and Florida. “Dr. Beach” looks at water temperature, natural beauty, sand quality and more.
articles.body: A crescent-shaped beach in Hawaii that’s immersed in greenery and facing an island just offshore is the best beach in the US. So says coastal scientist Stephen P. Leatherman, better known as “Dr. Beach.” Poipu Beach on the island of Kauai tops the list for 2026, which he compiles based on 50 individual criteria. The No. 2 beach, according to Leatherman’s annual ranking, is St. Andrews State Park in Panama City, Florida. Hawaii and Florida dominate the top 10, which includes Caladesi Island State Park in the Dunedin/Clearwater area of Florida, and Wailea Beach on the Hawaiian island of Maui. One beach in the Northeast broke into the top five: Main Beach in the picturesque eastern Long Island town of East Hampton. The New York beach ranked No. 5 this year. Leatherman notes the beach’s “peaceful, countryside setting in a small village” and the “towering sand dunes” that help make it so bucolic. Hawaii and Florida typically fare well in the ranking partly because Leatherman focuses on “swimming beaches,” which means the water has to be warm enough to draw people in for a few strokes. Beaches in Maine, Connecticut and other Northeastern states, for example, are often too “nippy” to make the cut, he said in an interview with CNN. One Massachusetts beach, however, caps off the top 10: Cape Cod’s Coast Guard Beach. Leatherman says visitors go by bike or shuttle bus to reach this pristine beach where in recent years seals have begun to congregate. Several beaches are located in private resorts, including Kaunaoa in Hawaii, also known as Mauna Kea Beach, located on the island of Hawaii. While the beach is located inside the Mauna Key Beach Resort, the shoreline is accessible through dint of the public right of way, stressed Leatherman, who teaches at Florida International University in Miami. Water temperature and clarity Don’t see your favorite beach? Water temperature, as noted, is likely the culprit. Leatherman says there are many spots he likes in Washington State, Northern California and Oregon, among other places, and he often hears from beachgoers who complain when these areas don’t make the list. “It’s just too bloody cold,” he said. Other factors that keep beaches off his ranking include tidal movements. Leatherman said strong tides make the water cloudy, which doesn’t always appeal to beachgoers because once immersed in the surf, “People want to see their toes.” Leatherman regularly cites beaches that have to be removed from the top 10 because of pollution or other issues. Three beaches were excluded from this year’s ranking, including Coronado Beach in San Diego for a second year in a row. Leatherman says sewage from the Tijuana River is gravely impacting the beach. “It is wrecking that whole area,” Leatherman said. “I am so upset about that.” San Diego County has repeatedly had to issue advisories due to the presence of bacteria in the water, warning swimmers to keep away. New advisories citing sewage from the Tijuana River were issued in May. The two other beaches that are off the list this year are Lighthouse Beach on the Outer Banks of North Carolina, due to erosion, and Cape Florida State Park in Miami where the vast quantity of sargassum seaweed washing up on shore is reducing the beach’s natural beauty. Leatherman has been publishing the annual list since 1991. The 50 criteria that he uses to evaluate the beaches include water and sand quality, the size of waves, the shape of the beach, cleanliness and rainfall. He “retires” beaches from his ranking so that other spots have a chance but that doesn’t mean there’s been a dip in quality. Last year, for example, Coopers Beach in the New York town of Southampton topped the list. He said it remains a wonderful beach. In the 2025 ranking, this year’s No. 1 beach, Poipu, came in third. There are 650 major public recreational beaches in the US, according to Dr. Beach, and he says he’s visited all of them. Top 10 US beaches for 2026

articles.title: Young people wanted community. They got 'eventslop.'
articles.summary: Are all these strange gatherings designed to go viral fostering togetherness or algorithm slop?
articles.body:
If you spend any time on social media, chances are a wacky or oddly specific event has hit your feed at some point in the last couple of years: A celebrity lookalike contest , a meetup for Wasian people , an aura battle among teenagers , an invitation to eat pudding with a fork with strangers.

The list goes on. But is this rash of viral gatherings in major metropolitan areas a sign that the masses are feeling more whimsical these days , or that human interaction is becoming more superficial, manufactured to feed an algorithm?

Adam Aleksic , a linguist and author of Algospeak: How Social Media Is Transforming the Future of Language , posed a theory on TikTok.

"People don't host real public gatherings anymore; they host 'eventslop,' where the main purpose of the event is to generate algorithmic engagement above all else," Aleksic, who goes by etymologynerd on TikTok, said in the video .

Aleksic noted that these events have largely been organized by influencers and suggested they were designed to be filmed "less to create social connections, and more to serve as a free laugh track for whatever crazy stunt is currently happening." They also rely on trending buzzwords, like "aura" and " Wasian ," he said, meaning they were "very likely orchestrated for algorithmic momentum."

Viral events are nothing new — I vividly remember receiving dozens of invites to bizarre gatherings on Facebook in the 2000s and 2010s, like pillow fight flash mobs and a plot to storm Area 51 — but there's no denying that they feel more common and social media-friendly now.

In this era of AI dominance, "slop" became a slang term for low-quality content created by the technology, but has since broadened to describe anything lazily produced. Aleksic said that while these events are probably plenty of fun, they're still "degraded versions of what they could have been" because the organizer's goal is to extract views from the public's desire for community.

One gathering that Aleksic cited as an example of eventslop is the 2024 Timothée Chalamet lookalike contest , which was followed by many other copycat contests, including one for the Heated Rivalry cast and another for New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani .

Content creator Anthony Po was responsible for starting the trend and has a knack for making events go viral. (Remember when a masked guy ate a jar of cheeseballs in front of a crowd ? That was him.)

Po told the Hollywood Reporter in 2024 that for the Chalamet lookalike contest, he considered, "What would be fun? What would get people talking?"

"Wholesome fun things that are free for people to gawk at and tell their grandkids about," he said, answering his own question.

Going viral certainly appeared to be the point. Po said he spent more than $4,000 on the event, flew in a judge and hired production assistants. He was also expecting a crowd and had a hunch that the real Chalamet could show up, but the chaos was a happy surprise. It's likely the contest wouldn't have gone viral if it weren't zeitgeisty and fun. Whimsy was integral to its success.

Gael Aitor, who organizes play-focused events for the social club Grownkid — like a " fight your evil situationship " rave in Los Angeles — argues that young people actually crave eventslop.

"Youth no longer want to be just consumers of content but rather part of the creation process itself, going offline to have a reason to enjoy the online again," he wrote in a February post on Grownkid's Substack . "With slop events, both sides win. Creators get a steady stream of moments to turn into long-form content and spread through clips, and attendees get to help create it while connecting with their communities."

People crave community. The loneliness epidemic among Gen Zers has been widely covered, as has the dwindling number of third spaces where people can gather. We might be more connected to each other and our interests thanks to social media, but in-person interactions still offer something uniquely valuable.

If lookalike contests and aura battles feel too inauthentic for your taste, there are plenty of other quirky gatherings where you'll find community. Axios reported that there's been an increase in people gathering around shared hobbies like mahjong and silent reading. And according to Eventbrite , there's also been an increase in "soft socializing," where people get together to make connections naturally, without necessarily having the goal of networking. Some concerts have banned phones, encouraging attendees to live in the moment.

What viral events and phone-free ones have in common is this: People know what they're getting into when they go. When attending something you found on social media that seems buzzy and of-the-moment, it's pretty obvious that it'll involve creating content. But offline soirees are still possible too. Consider the fact that we still don't know what Taylor Swift's wedding dress looks like.

Therapist Lynn Zakeri told Yahoo that the rise of eventslop might not be such a bad thing. Attending often requires bravery and social interaction.

"Look at it like this: You got out of the house, made eye contact with someone and made a new friend," she said. "If you want to be there as a hater, go do it! Take a risk. Do whatever you want to do."

Dressing up, going somewhere and mingling with others are all part of joining a community, and the end goal of going viral doesn't necessarily diminish that.

articles.title: MPF investiga DSEI Yanomami por irregularidades em tratamento para 'bicho-de-pé' | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação ocorre após vistoria presencial identificar problemas no estoque e na distribuição de remeédios para o tratamento do parasita no distrito sanitário local.
articles.summary: Investigação ocorre após vistoria presencial identificar problemas no estoque e na distribuição de remeédios para o tratamento do parasita no distrito sanitário local.
articles.body:
Mão de criança yanomami com tungíase. Foto tirada em janeiro de 2022 na comunidade Yaritobi, parte do território yanomami — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Carla C F Rodrigues

O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) instaurou, nesta quinta-feira (3), uma i nvestigação para apurar irregularidades na gestão de medicamentos usados no tratamento da tungíase , doença conhecida como bicho-de-pé , na Terra Indígena Yanomami , em Roraima.

Em nota, o Ministério da Saúde informou que "não há medicamentos com validade vencida disponíveis para uso no Distrito Sanitário Especial Indígena (DSEI) Yanomami, conforme verificação realizada nesta quinta-feira (3)".

A investigação iniciou após uma inspeção na sede do Distrito Sanitário Especial Indígena (DSEI) Yanomami. A ação verifica se a compra, o armazenamento, a rotulagem, o registro e a distribuição dos medicamentos seguem as normas.

O MPF também vai apurar suspeitas de uso de remédios com prazo de validade vencido , falhas no registro dos produtos nos sistemas oficiais de controle, se o abastecimento de medicamentos e a assistência prestada aos indígenas são suficientes.

O Dsei-YY é um órgão do Ministério da Saúde e responsável pela saúde dos povos do território Yanomami.

A portaria sobre a instigação é assinada pelo procurador da república Alisson Marugal e foi publicada no diário oficial do MPF.

A doença é causada por uma pulga fêmea , que gosta de ambientes secos e solos arenosos, e se alimenta do sangue de humanos e de animais.

O parasita entra na pele por qualquer parte do corpo que está em contato com o chão - principalmente pés, mãos e nádegas - causando, como primeiros sinais, irritação e coceira.

Uma vez dentro do corpo, o parasita, se não for retirado a tempo, coloca seus ovos na pele, e a i nfecção se alastra . As lesões causadas pela tungíase podem ser únicas ou bastante numerosas, dependendo da infestação do solo.

A Terra Yanomami é o maior território indígena do Brasil, com quase 10 milhões de hectares entre Roraima, Amazonas e parte da Venezuela. Garimpeiros atuam na região desde, ao menos, a década de 1970.

Até dezembro de 2025, o garimpo ilegal destruiu 5.564 hectares da Terra Yanomami, segundo o levantamento. A maior parte da destruição ocorreu antes de 2023, ano em que o governo federal decretou situação de emergência .

articles.summary: Incêndio foi registrado na noite desta quinta-feira (3), na altura do Km 108 da rodovia. Não há registro de feridos.
articles.body:
Uma carreta que transportava calçados ficou destruída após pegar fogo na noite desta quinta-feira (3), na Rodovia Presidente Dutra, em Taubaté . Não houve registro de feridos.

De acordo com a concessionária RioSP, o incêndio foi registrado por volta das 23h24, na altura do km 108 da rodovia, na pista sentido Rio de Janeiro.

Equipes da concessionária foram acionadas para a ocorrência, além do Corpo de Bombeiros. As chamas foram controladas cerca de 20 minutos depois.

A concessionária informou ainda que houve interdição de uma das faixas e do acostamento e que houve um congestionamento de 3 quilômetros.

articles.title: Exposição Muralha da China em Campinas tem entrada gratuita | G1
articles.standfirst: Percurso da exposição usa projeções, recursos táteis e jogos interativos para explorar da construção até os dias atuais do monumento. Instalada no Instituto CPFL, mostra fica em cartaz até 31 de outubro.
articles.summary: Percurso da exposição usa projeções, recursos táteis e jogos interativos para explorar da construção até os dias atuais do monumento. Mostra fica em cartaz até 31 de outubro.
articles.body:
#paratodosverem: Montagem com três fotografias relacionadas à exposição "A Grande Muralha da China". À esquerda, uma imagem mostra um trecho da Grande Muralha da China, com caminho de pedras e torre ao fundo. Ao centro, sobre uma mesa de madeira, há dois recipientes claros com ervas e sementes secas espalhadas ao redor, diante de um painel ilustrado. À direita, uma escultura de dragão colorida ocupa parte de uma sala expositiva com iluminação artificial. O dragão tem corpo em tons de vermelho, azul e amarelo, boca aberta e detalhes ornamentais na cabeça — Foto: Isadora de Paiva

Com projeções e efeitos sensoriais, uma exposição imersiva faz o visitante caminhar pela "Grande Muralha da China" sem sair de Campinas (SP). Com entrada gratuita, a mostra fica no Instituto CPFL até 31 de outubro - veja detalhes abaixo.

Segundo os organizadores, o objetivo da exposição é apresentar a construção, a cultura chinesa e as transformações do monumento ao longo dos séculos. Para isso, o espaço usa projeções em grande escala, sons, recursos táteis e jogos interativos.

Criado pela empresa YDreams Global, o percurso é dividido em ambientes inspirados na metáfora do "Dragão de Pedra que Nunca Dorme", figura usada para representar a Muralha.

Segundo a curadora Karina Israel, cada sala apresenta uma parte dessa narrativa.

“A gente descobriu que a Muralha da China é vista como um grande dragão de pedra. Então, fizemos essa metáfora e cada sala é um ponto de vista dessa história”, explica.

A visitação passa por diferentes fases da história do monumento. Veja como os ambientes são divididos:

😴 Dragão adormecido: O primeiro espaço apresenta a origem da Muralha. Ele mostra que a obra não surgiu de uma só vez, mas a partir de fragmentos erguidos ao longo de séculos.

🐉 Corpo do dragão: Reúne informações sobre os materiais de construção, a Rota da Seda e réplicas de objetos. O local também tem jogos interativos. Um deles aborda mitos, como a ideia de que o monumento poderia ser visto da Lua.

💗 Coração do dragão: É o ponto mais imersivo. Projeções, sons e efeitos sensoriais recriam as paisagens atravessadas pela Muralha, dando ao visitante a sensação de estar dentro da construção.

🐲 Alma do dragão: A última parte mostra o papel do monumento na atualidade. O espaço reúne referências a festivais e maratonas realizados no local. Há também a instalação de um grande dragão e um simulador de corrida.

A imersão despertou lembranças na advogada chinesa Sara Hong Zha, que conheceu a exposição durante a inauguração para convidados. Ela vive no Brasil e já visitou a estrutura original com a família.

“Essa exposição me fez relembrar aquela época, a grandiosidade da natureza e da Muralha. É muito fiel”, conta.

➡️ A mostra conta com recursos de acessibilidade, como mapa tátil e apoio para pessoas cegas ou com baixa visão. Há também profissionais da Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) disponíveis durante as visitas.

O evento integra a 10ª edição do Intercâmbio Brasil-China do Instituto CPFL e faz parte da programação do Ano da Cultura China-Brasil, celebrado em 2026.

Local: Instituto CPFL, Rua Jorge de Figueiredo Corrêa, 1.632, Chácara Primavera, Campinas (SP)

Período: de 3 de setembro a 31 de outubro

Horários: segunda, terça, quarta e sexta, das 8h às 17h; quinta, das 8h às 19h; sábado, das 10h às 16h

#paratodosverem: Em ambiente interno amplo e com iluminação baixa, uma estrutura cenográfica em formato de dragão ocupa o centro da sala. O corpo longo e sinuoso, na cor vermelha, atravessa o espaço de um lado ao outro. Na extremidade direita está a cabeça do dragão, com detalhes dourados e feixe intenso de luz vermelha saindo da região da boca. À esquerda, uma pessoa adulta observa a instalação e segura um telefone celular apontado para a peça. Ao fundo, há painéis expositivos, paredes decoradas e pontos de luz no teto. A estrutura faz parte da exposição imersiva "A Grande Muralha da China", no Instituto CPFL, em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

*Estagiária sob supervisão de Bárbara Camilotti e Fernando Evans.

articles.title: Vídeo mostra agressão que deixou criança autista com braço fraturado em clínica de São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Paciente passou por cirurgia de urgência no cotovelo e ficou 30 dias em recuperação. Investigado foi demitido do estabelecimento e indiciado.
articles.summary: Paciente passou por cirurgia de urgência no cotovelo e ficou 30 dias em recuperação. Investigado foi demitido do estabelecimento e indiciado.
articles.body:
Uma criança autista e não verbal sofreu uma fratura grave no braço direito após ser arremessada ao chão durante uma sessão terapêutica em uma clínica particular de São Luís . O caso aconteceu em 24 de julho, mas ganhou repercussão nos últimos dias, após a divulgação de imagens de uma câmera de segurança.

Nas imagens, um homem aparece interagindo com a criança durante o atendimento ( assista acima ). Em determinado momento, ele a arremessa contra o chão. A vítima deixou a clínica chorando e com o braço machucado, segundo a família.

De acordo com a família, os exames constataram uma fratura grave. Por causa da lesão, a criança precisou passar por uma cirurgia de urgência no cotovelo e permaneceu 30 dias em recuperação . Somente agora ela está retomando a rotina de atividades.

Após o registro do boletim de ocorrência pela família, o homem que aparece nas imagens foi demitido pela clínica e indiciado por lesão corporal de natureza grave, segundo a delegada responsável pela investigação. A função que ele exercia no local não foi informada.

A pena prevista para esse crime é de um a cinco anos de reclusão. O inquérito foi concluído e encaminhado à Justiça em 15 de agosto.

O caso está sob análise do Ministério Público do Maranhão e tramita em segredo de Justiça.

articles.summary: Expediente nas repartições públicas vai ser encerrado nesta sexta-feira (4), e retomado na terça-feira (8). Veja funcionamento de comércio e serviços públicos.
articles.body:
Imagem da Av. Norte-Sul e parte do Cambuí, em Campinas (SP) — Foto: Carlos Bassan/Prefeitura de Campinas

Com o feriado da Indenpendência do Brasil, celebrado na segunda-feira (7), alguns serviços públicos, o comércio e horas de lazer adotam horários de funcionamento diferenciados em Campinas (SP).

O expediente nas repartições públicas encerra-se nesta sexta-feira (4), e será retomado na terça-feira (8). Já os serviços essenciais funcionam em esquema de plantão.

O g1 preparou uma lista com o que abre e o que fecha durante o feriado. Confira, abaixo, o levantamento.

Praças de Esportes: fechadas na segunda-feira (7);

Operação Lagoa: das 7h às 12h, no domingo (6) e não abre na segunda-feira (7);

Ciclofaixa de Lazer Taquaral/Norte-Sul: das 7h às 13h, no domingo (6).

articles.title: Jogos escolares valorizam cultura ribeirinha em Belém | G1
articles.standfirst: Competição da Escola Milton Monte reúne cerca de 140 estudantes com modalidades esportivas inspiradas nas tradições e no cotidiano das comunidades tradicionais da floresta.
articles.summary: Competição da Escola Milton Monte reúne cerca de 140 estudantes com modalidades esportivas inspiradas nas tradições e no cotidiano das comunidades tradicionais da floresta.
articles.body:
Estudantes competem para ver quem sobe e desce mais rápido do açaizeiro — Foto: Paula Lourinho/ Agência Belém

Subir no açaizeiro, apostar corrida de canoa e arremessar ouriços de castanha-do-pará são atividades realizadas pelos estudantes da Ilha do Combu, em Belém , durante a 12ª edição dos Jogos do Território e da Ancestralidade.

🔎 A ilha do Combu é a quarta maior das 39 que compõem a região insular de Belém . Região ribeirinha, é destino de muitos turistas que procuram gastronomia paraense e banho de rio em restaurantes de palafitas às margens da Baía do Guajará.

Longe das quadras esportivas tradicionais, os alunos ribeirinhos participam de provas baseadas em práticas reais do cotidiano e do território, como apanhar açaí e canoagem.

Os jogos são na Escola Municipal de Educação do Campo (Emec) Milton Monte, reunindo cerca de 140 alunos da região das ilhas. A competição segue com programações até esta sexta-feira (4).

As atividades incluem modalidades típicas da rotina ribeirinha, como:

Corrida do boco (brincadeira com a palha que se desprende do açaizeiro);

Arremesso de cacau e de ouriço (inspirado no arremesso de disco);

Confecção da peconha (alça de fibra usada nos pés para subir em árvores);

Debulhagem do açaí, corrida de canoa, pesca com caniço e natação no rio.

Os Jogos do Território e da Ancestralidade são inspirados no cotidiano e nas tradições das comunidades ribeirinhas — Foto: Paula Lourinho/ Agência Belém

De acordo com o coordenador pedagógico da escola, Jenijunior Santos, a iniciativa busca valorizar a identidade cultural local e fortalecer o vínculo das crianças com os saberes passados de geração em geração .

“Estamos em uma escola do campo, no contexto do território ribeirinho, onde as pessoas vivem e transformam suas vidas a partir da realidade da natureza onde estão”, afirma o coordenador.

O coordenador pedagógico da escola, Jenijunior Santos, diz que os jogos estão em uma intrínseca relação com o cotidiano das populações ribeirinhas — Foto: Paula Lourinho/ Agência Belém

Para Kauane Maia, de 11 anos, aluna do 5º ano da escola Milton Monte, os jogos ajudam a reforçar o aprendizado de tarefas diárias.

“Está sendo muito legal, porque a gente aprende mais na escola e dá para a gente ajudar os nossos pais quando for remar para buscar água”, conta.

Além das provas ligadas à tradição ribeirinha, a programação de quatro dias conta com atividades esportivas e recreativas tradicionais, como salto em distância, cabo de guerra, futebol, queimada e jogos de mesa.

Corrida de canoa a remo foi uma das modalidades disputadas nos jogos — Foto: Paula Lourinho/ Agência Belém

articles.title: Itaquá Rodeio Fest: Gusttavo Lima e Henrique & Juliano lideram ranking | G1

articles.summary: O Itaquá Rodeio Fest começa neste sábado com um levantamento sobre a popularidade de Gusttavo Lima, Henrique & Juliano e outras atrações nas plataformas digitais.
articles.body:
Itaquá Rodeio Fest tem 13 atrações este ano — Foto: Divulgação/g1

O Itaquá Rodeio Fest 2026 começa neste sábado (5) com shows de Gusttavo Lima, Sorriso Maroto e Matuê. Ao todo, 13 atrações vão passar pelo evento, que será realizado durante dois fins de semana em comemoração aos 466 anos de Itaquaquecetuba.

📲🎧 Mas quem é o artista mais ouvido do festival? E quem tem mais seguidores? Um levantamento feito pelo g1 mostra a presença dos nomes confirmados na programação nas plataformas digitais.

Henrique e Juliano lideram entre os artistas mais ouvidos, com 16,1 milhões de ouvintes mensais. Gusttavo Lima aparece logo depois, com 15,1 milhões, seguido por Panda, que soma 14,7 milhões.

Já entre os mais seguidos, Gusttavo Lima ocupa a primeira posição, com 45,2 milhões de seguidores. Simone Mendes vem em seguida, com 40 milhões, enquanto Henrique e Juliano aparecem na terceira colocação, com 18,7 milhões.

Juntas, as atrações somam mais de 115,5 milhões de ouvintes mensais e aproximadamente 158,4 milhões de seguidores.

🤠 O sertanejo é o gênero com maior presença na programação, com seis atrações: Gusttavo Lima, Panda, Simone Mendes, Gustavo Mioto, Henrique & Juliano e Bia Frazzo.

🥁🪗 O festival também reúne Sorriso Maroto e Belo, do pagode; Grelo e Natanzinho Lima, do arrocha; Matuê, do trap; Filho do Piseiro, do piseiro; e Calcinha Preta, do forró.

Raio-x das atrações do Itaquá Rodeio Fest 2026

O levantamento considera o número de ouvintes mensais e de seguidores de cada atração. Os dados foram consultados nesta quinta-feira (3) e podem sofrer alterações.

O Itaquá Rodeio Fest acontece nos dias 5, 6, 11 e 12 de setembro. Confira a programação:

5 de setembro (sábado): Gusttavo Lima, Sorriso Maroto e Matuê;

6 de setembro (domingo): Simone Mendes, Panda, Gustavo Mioto e Filho do Piseiro;

11 de setembro (sexta-feira): Henrique e Juliano, Grelo e Bia Frazzo;

12 de setembro (sábado): Natanzinho Lima, Belo e Calcinha Preta.

Os interessados puderam trocar ingressos para a pista por alimentos não perecíveis. A ação aconteceu entre os dias 10 e 30 de agosto.

Os ingressos também estão disponíveis para compra no site oficial do evento.

articles.title: Mãe e irmã de homem torturado por PMs devem ganhar R$ 45 mil no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão determina indenização de R$ 30 mil para a mãe e R$ 15 mil para a irmã de Sandro José Vidal da Silva, torturado em 2018 por três policiais militares em Rio Branco.
articles.summary: Decisão determina indenização de R$ 30 mil para a mãe e R$ 15 mil para a irmã de Sandro José Vidal da Silva, torturado em 2018 por três policiais militares em Rio Branco.
articles.body:
A mãe e irmã de Sandro José Vidal da Silva, torturado por três policiais militares em 2018 , em Rio Branco , devem ganhar R$ 45 mil em indenizações por danos morais. A Justiça condenou o Estado a pagar R$ 30 mil para a mãe da vítima e R$ 15 mil para a irmã dele.

A decisão reconheceu que a violência praticada pelos policiais causou sofrimento à família e que o caso ultrapassou os limites de uma abordagem policial. Sandro morreu em novembro de 2024, mais de seis anos depois da tortura, após sofrer um acidente de trânsito.

O g1 entrou em contato com o governo do estado e, até a última atualização desta reportagem, não obteve retorno.

👉 Contexto: As agressões ocorreram em fevereiro de 2018, no bairro Aeroporto Velho, em Rio Branco. Sandro foi abordado pelos policiais militares Ângelo Gleiwitz Moreira Siriano, Leonardo Lima e Lima e Nilando da Silva Diniz. Os três militares foram condenados por tortura e a sentença nessa ação foi definitiva em novembro de 2021.

Ao g1 , Maryna Vidal da Silva, irmã de Sandro, informou que a família já foi notificada da decisão pelo defensor público que acompanha o caso. Ela disse que todos ainda tentam assimilar o resultado.

Ela contou também que a mãe ainda lembra de Sandro todos os dias e que o estado de saúde dela torna o momento ainda mais difícil.

“Parece que não houve nenhum tipo de Justiça porque só agora saiu um resultado, depois de anos”, afirmou.

José Vidal da Silva, torturado por três policiais militares em fevereiro de 2018, em Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Segundo a denúncia do Ministério Público do Acre (MP-AC), Sandro foi abordado pelos policiais militares Ângelo Gleiwitz Moreira Siriano, Leonardo Lima e Lima e Nilando da Silva Diniz.

De acordo com a acusação, os policiais deram socos, chutes e golpes de cassetete em Sandro, além de fazer ameaças psicológicas . A vítima também foi levada para as margens do rio, onde foi obrigada a se deitar na lama.

Mesmo depois de Sandro dizer que não sabia nadar, os policiais o fizeram pular no rio, segundo a denúncia. As agressões causaram lesões graves e fraturas pelo corpo.

Na época, o MP-AC denunciou os três policiais pelo crime de tortura e pediu, além da condenação, a reparação dos danos causados à vítima e a perda dos cargos públicos.

Os militares foram presos em maio de 2019. Naquele mesmo ano, a Justiça manteve a prisão preventiva dos três. Em 2021, a Câmara Criminal do Tribunal de Justiça do Acre manteve a condenação.

As penas somavam mais de 19 anos de prisão, inicialmente em regime semiaberto. As defesas chegaram a pedir que o crime de tortura fosse desclassificado para lesão corporal e também a redução das penas, mas os pedidos não foram acolhidos.

Além disso, a ação foi movida pela mãe e pela irmã de Sandro contra o Estado. No processo, elas alegaram que as agressões deixaram danos físicos e psicológicos na vítima e também causaram sofrimento à família.

O Estado contestou o pedido e alegou, entre outros pontos, que a ação havia sido apresentada fora do prazo. A Justiça rejeitou esse argumento porque a tortura também foi investigada e julgada na esfera criminal.

Na sentença, o juiz considerou que não havia mais discussão sobre a ocorrência da tortura ou sobre a participação dos policiais , já que esses pontos foram reconhecidos de forma definitiva pela Justiça.

Estado é condenado a indenizar em R$ 45 mil família de homem torturado por PMs no Acre — Foto: Lopes/Seinfra

Sandro morreu em 11 de novembro de 2024, mais de seis anos depois da tortura. Ele sofreu um acidente de trânsito e morreu em decorrência de um choque neurogênico.

A Justiça deixou claro que a morte não teve relação comprovada com as agressões de 2018 . Por isso, o Estado não foi condenado a pagar indenização pelo falecimento nem uma pensão à família.

O pedido de pensionamento também foi negado porque não houve comprovação suficiente de que a mãe ou a irmã dependessem financeiramente de Sandro.

A indenização de R$ 45 mil, portanto, é referente somente aos danos morais provocados pela tortura. Os valores ainda terão correção monetária e juros.

articles.title: Doceria asiática de Sorocaba aposta em sobremesas divertidas | G1
articles.standfirst: Doceria familiar inaugurada em Sorocaba (SP) aposta em sobremesas asiáticas divertidas para todas as idades. O destaque do menu é o taiyaki, bolo japonês em formato de peixe que serve como cone.
articles.summary: Doceria de Sorocaba é um projeto familiar inaugurado há poucas semanas, tem como principal receita o taiyaki, bolo japonês em formato de peixe que serve como "cone" para sorvete.
articles.body:
Depois do almoço, em um dia triste, durante a TPM ou após uma consulta médica, a verdade é uma só: um doce cai bem a qualquer hora. Em Sorocaba , no interior de São Paulo, a experiência de comer uma sobremesa se transformou em uma viagem cultural em uma doceria com menu inspirado na culinária asiática.

A doceria Taiyaki Candy, projeto familiar inaugurado há poucas semanas, tem como principal receita o taiyaki — um bolo japonês em formato de peixe que serve como "cone" para sorvetes e outros recheios.

Ao g1 , a proprietária, Miriam de Oliveira Nagaishi, contou que o marido, a filha e a enteada também fazem parte da equipe, cada um com uma função específica dentro da empresa.

"Eu sempre gostei da área de produção de sobremesas, mas até então era mais como um hobby, nunca tinha pensado em transformar isso em um negócio. Minha filha sempre me pedia para irmos à Liberdade, em São Paulo, e fomos algumas vezes. Foi nessas visitas que comecei a ter contato com esse universo de sobremesas asiáticas e a ideia foi surgindo", disse.

Proprietária da doceria de Sorocaba (SP), Miriam de Oliveira Nagaishi, e sua família — Foto: Taiyaki Candy/Reprodução

Decidida a abrir o negócio, Miriam pesquisou sobre o segmento na região e, pela originalidade do projeto, investiu em produtos, máquinas e fornecedores necessários para a inauguração.

Além da inspiração turística, há uma forte ligação cultural na família. Miriam tem ascendência japonesa, e tanto os irmãos quanto o pai moraram muitos anos no Japão.

"De certa forma, trazer um pouco dessa cultura para o nosso negócio também tem um significado especial para a nossa família", pontua.

A família já havia atuado no comércio, mas em outro segmento. A doceria surgiu da vontade de fazer algo diferente, que transmitisse a identidade familiar e fosse além da venda de sobremesas, proporcionando uma experiência nova ao público.

A escolha do cardápio ocorreu, principalmente, pelo desejo de oferecer uma experiência inédita na região. A ideia foi aproveitar o apelo visual e divertido dos doces, fugindo do tradicional sorvete expresso.

O formato do taiyaki, por exemplo, atrai o público justamente por ser uma novidade para a maioria das pessoas. O "cone" de peixinho possui uma abertura para ser recheado com sorvete e toppings — ingredientes adicionados por cima para realçar o sabor, a textura e a aparência.

Semelhante às massas de waffles ou panquecas, a receita leva farinha, ovos, açúcar, leite, fermento e água, destacando-se por ser mais leve e fluida.

"Ao mesmo tempo, procuramos adaptar os produtos ao paladar do nosso público. Temos sabores e combinações, mais conhecidos, como creme de avelã, biscoito de baunilha e chocolate ao leite com avelã, mas também buscamos trazer novidades e combinações diferentes. Nosso objetivo é justamente unir a inspiração asiática com sabores que façam sentido para os nossos clientes", explica a empreendedora.

Para ela, o equilíbrio entre o visual diferenciado, a experiência e o sabor é o que torna a proposta única.

Doceria de Sorocaba (SP) oferece viagem cultural com menu inspirado na culinária asiática — Foto: Taiyaki Candy/Reprodução

Dar uma mordida no peixinho ou nos doces em formato de panda atrai não apenas crianças, mas também adultos. Miriam relata que se surpreendeu com a diversidade do público, que atrai desde adolescentes até famílias inteiras.

"As crianças realmente ficam encantadas com os formatos e com a apresentação dos produtos, mas os adultos também demonstram muita curiosidade. Muitas vezes a pessoa chega porque viu algo diferente no Instagram ou passou em frente à loja e ficou curiosa para saber o que é", contou.

As opções do cardápio incluem o Taiyaki Tradicional, o Taiyaki Panda, o Taiyaki Oreo e o Taiyaki Bueno, apontado como o "queridinho" do público. Os clientes também podem montar o próprio taiyaki, escolhendo sabores, caldas e toppings.

Estão disponíveis, ainda, o cascão panda, o bubble candy e o bubble waffle , acompanhados de frutas, chocolates e outros complementos.

Os s’mores asiáticos são outro destaque. Eles se assemelham aos tradicionais — uma espécie de "sanduíche" de biscoitos recheados com marshmallow assado e uma camada de chocolate. A versão asiática, no entanto, incorpora ingredientes com sabores diferenciados, como matcha e melão verde.

O cardápio, segundo Miriam, está em constante evolução, com testes de novos produtos conforme a demanda.

"É uma sensação muito especial ver a satisfação dos clientes. Ficamos muito felizes e agradecidos com a reação de cada cliente que passa por aqui. Como é um negócio familiar, colocamos muito carinho em tudo o que fazemos. Então, quando vemos uma pessoa experimentando pela primeira vez, ficando surpresa com o produto, tirando fotos, comentando que gostou, ou voltando para experimentar novamente, é muito gratificante", finaliza.

articles.title: Veja o que vai funcionar durante o feriado prolongado no Tocantins  | G1

articles.summary: Feriados da Independência do Brasil e de Nossa Senhora da Natividade formam um período de até quatro dias de folga. Confira o funcionamento dos principais serviços em Palmas.
articles.body:
Cidade de Palmas (TO) — Foto: Adilvan Nogueira/Governo do Tocantins

Quem pretende aproveitar o feriadão de 7 e 8 de setembro precisa ficar atento às mudanças no funcionamento de serviços no Tocantins. Os dois feriados, um nacional e outro estadual, serão celebrados na segunda e na terça-feira e quem não trabalha no fim de semana pode garantir até quatro dias de folga.

O comércio, os serviços de saúde e os órgãos públicos terão horários ou funcionamento diferenciados durante o período. Confira o que abre e fecha.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

No dia 7 de setembro, Dia da Independência, não haverá abertura do comércio em geral, conforme previsto na Convenção Coletiva de Trabalho 2024/2026, segundo a Federação do Comércio do Tocantins (Fecomércio-TO).

Estabelecimentos instalados em shoppings e de gêneros alimentícios poderão abrir, com pagamento das horas trabalhadas em dobro ou compensação.

No dia 8, Dia da Padroeira do Tocantins, o comércio em geral poderá funcionar. O pagamento de horas extras será devido somente após o cumprimento da jornada normal de trabalho.

Em Palmas, as Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPAs) Norte e Sul funcionarão normalmente durante os dois feriados, 24 horas por dia. O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu 192) também manterá o atendimento normalmente.

As Unidades de Saúde da Família (USFs) e os Postinhos Corujinhas ficarão fechados, com duas exceções:

USF Walter Pereira Morato, em Taquaruçu: atendimento 24 horas;

USF Mariazinha Rodrigues da Silva, em Buritirana: atendimento das 7h às 18h.

Em Taquaruçu, a unidade 24 horas terá equipe reforçada durante os quatro dias de festival realizado no distrito. Segundo a Prefeitura de Palmas, os demais serviços ambulatoriais e administrativos da rede municipal de saúde retomam o funcionamento na quarta-feira (9).

Segundo a Febraban, as agências bancárias não estarão abertas para atendimento presencial no feriado de 7 de setembro. Compensações bancárias, incluindo TED, não serão efetivadas nessa data. O PIX funcionará normalmente, 24 horas. Na terça-feira (8) o atendimento segue normalmente nas localidades onde não é feriado ou ponto facultativo.

Boletos e contas de consumo (água, energia, telefone) com vencimento no dia (7) poderão ser pagos sem acréscimo no próximo dia útil. No caso de tributos e impostos, o pagamento deve ser antecipado para evitar juros e multa.

Lojas secas: das 11h às 17h (Horario de domingo)

Lojas secas e Praças de alimentação: 10h às 22h

Não haverá atendimento nas agências dos correios nos dias 7 e 8 de setembro. O atendimento retorna normalmente na quarta-feira, dia 9.

Os supermercados Gigante e Big funcionarão normalmente, sem alteração de horário. O supermercado Quartetto funciona em horário de domingo, fechando mais cedo, na segunda-feira e na terça-feira funciona em horário normal.

articles.title: Dia da Independência: veja desfiles cívicos na região de Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do g1 reúne programação das comemorações do 7 de setembro em Piracicaba (SP), Limeira (SP), Santa Bárbara d’Oeste (SP), Nova Odessa (SP), Cordeirópolis (SP), Charqueada (SP), Rafard (SP), São Pedro (SP) e Elias Fausto (SP).
articles.summary: Levantamento do g1 reúne programação das comemorações do 7 de setembro.
articles.body:
Estudantes de São Pedro (SP) em Desfile do Dia da Independência do Brasil — Foto: Tiago Stoco

articles.title: Two men pulled alive from Nepal hydropower plant tunnel nine days after floods
articles.summary: The dramatic breakthrough comes after voices were heard from inside the tunnels of the stricken plant. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Workers rescued: Two people have been pulled alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal, more than a week after catastrophic floods at its border with China. The plant was unrecognizable from the disaster, and rescuers had to use satellite pictures to find it below the mud.

• Survivor’s account: Sanjay Sah, 30, who is in a stable condition, had to ask rescuers what date it was . He said he was trapped after helping others escape and kept his spirits up chanting Hindu mantras. Kabir Maharjan, 45 is critically ill. Both are being treated in a hospital .

• Efforts continue: The discovery of the two has given rescuers renewed hope more can be saved. Hundreds of hydropower workers are missing from the disaster.

• Death toll: The number of people killed in Nepal has exceeded 1,290. The death toll in China was 21, according to its latest update on Wednesday. About 5,500 across both countries remain missing.

Let’s take a step back to assess ongoing emergency efforts in northern Nepal, where a team found two survivors from deluged underground tunnels following last week’s lethal floods.

The technical feat of the operation cannot be underestimated, according to Arnold Dix, a geologist in touch with crews on the ground.

“We’ve proven a concept for the first time ever in the history of these sorts of rescues in the world… a way to get people out alive,” Dix told CNN’s Salma Abdelaziz on CNN Newsroom Friday.

As teams make their way through the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station, Dix laid out a three-point action plan:

Finding evidence of the power station: The floods on August 26 “totally destroyed” the station, according to Dix, leaving “virtually no evidence” on the surface.

Goldilocks zones : Instead, researchers were tasked with analyzing engineering drawings of the station to try and identify areas where people might have survived, which Dix terms “Goldilocks zones.”

Locating survivors: An “earthwork operation” followed, Dix said, describing a process of draining water and rock from the tunnels, blowing a hole into the roof and eventually getting rescue staffers to dig inside the network “with their fingers” while crawling “on their bellies.”

What next? The two survivors – Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan – were found inside a cable tunnel, added Dix. Crews are now heading towards the power station itself, the geologist said, adding that they’re about 150 meters (492 feet) away. “That’s where we are hoping to find more people.”

While the rescue of two men in Nepal brought some rare good news on Friday, the broader situation in the country remains challenging, with thousands of people displaced and thousands of homes destroyed.

About 43,000 people in Nepal – roughly 10,000 families – are in need of immediate humanitarian relief, according to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), citing Nepali disaster management authorities.

Government estimates indicate that more than 84,000 people in Nepal have been affected by the flooding and landslides, according to the update .

Many of those affected are in hard-to-reach areas, and the UN food program said it has dispatched specialist logistics teams to help its humanitarian partners reach the most isolated locations.

“The disaster risks worsening existing nutrition challenges. Even before the floods, malnutrition, child wasting and anaemia rates were high in Nepal, with one in four children nationwide affected by stunting. Disrupted markets, lost livelihoods and reduced access to diverse and nutritious food could further increase nutrition risks,” WFP said.

Also taking off from the Nepal Army barracks at the Trishuli base this morning – a chopper airlifting a pregnant woman and her family to hospital.

The woman was brought into the barracks on a small vehicle and stretchered to an army tent. Around ten minutes later, she was flown out by chopper.

She had been unable to reach a local hospital following the flood, a military official told CNN, and she was facing complications.

For context: Thousands of people have been displaced in Nepal in the wake of the glacier collapse and catastrophic flooding. The Trishuli barracks has been operating as a staging area for civilians evacuated from the flood zones, until they can move on to temporary housing.

Nepali authorities estimate that the country will need to rebuild about 20,000 houses in flood-ravaged areas, with more than 7,500 homes destroyed.

The body of a third person has been recovered from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project just hours after two workers were found alive, the Nepal Electricity Authority says.

The deceased has been identified as Binod Pandey.

Suresh Raut, deputy manager at the Nepal Electricity Authority, who was at the rescue site when the body was discovered, said an 11-man team, including relatives of the missing, has been dispatched to search the surrounding area.

“Then, search and rescue in Trishuli 3A will be concluded,” Raut explained, adding: “We see less possibility of finding other missing people at this tunnel.”

The pulling of two men alive from a hydropower tunnel deep inside the Nepal Himalaya nine days after the disaster has sparked hope in Nepal.

The mood among rescuers is high. But reaching others still trapped in the tunnel — and whose condition is unknown — will be challenging.

The Nepal Army believes another 40 people are still inside the tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project. Their condition is not known.

Rescuers are using “various types of detectors, thermal detectors… elongated cameras, remotely piloted vehicles, drones of sorts,” Maj. Gen. Anup Jung Thapa, head of military operations, told CNN in an interview on Thursday.

In one of the tunnels there is a conduit for drainage of water, where the water is about 26 meters (85 feet) deep, he said.

Last week, CNN spoke to hydro workers from a nearby tunnel who spoke of water, cement and debris rushing through the darkness as the flood hit. They spoke of seeing the bodies of their colleagues wash past them as they struggled desperately to escape to the surface, more than 200 meters (656 feet) away. That escape took them six hours.

The area is incredibly remote and connectivity is limited, underscoring just how tough this rescue effort remains for those working day and night to save their friends and colleagues.

Throughout Friday, choppers took off and landing constantly from the Trishuli barracks.

On the walls outside the barracks are dozens of missing persons photos, illustrating the number of those still missing.

Two Nepali men were rescued alive after nine days trapped in a hydropower plant tunnel following the catastrophic flash flooding that hit on August 26. Rescuers have been working for more than a week at the site of the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant in the hopes of finding people alive.

Sanjay Sah, 30, and Kabir Maharjan, 45, were hauled out of the mud-filled tunnel on Friday morning. Both have been transferred to Birendra Army Hospital in Kathmandu.

Sah, a mechanical foreman, said in a video recorded from his hospital bed that on the day of the disaster, it took time for him to get others workers evacuated and that he didn’t have enough time to escape himself. “I don’t think everyone was able to escape. The tunnel is very long,” he added.

Sah, who is from Saptari district in eastern Nepal, is in stable condition. Maharjan, a mechanical supervisor from Kathmandu, is in critical condition and remains in intensive care, according to the Nepali Prime Minister’s Office.

Emergency workers told CNN at the site that they remain hopeful of finding more people alive. But the situation remains murky and operations are cumbersome, with rescuers digging by hand .

CNN has spoken to the father of 30-year-old survivor Sanjay Sah. His dad, Ramphal, said he initially “didn’t believe it.” “When I saw his photo, there was no limit to my happiness,” Ramphal said in an interview.

Nepali authorities have previously said there are more than 900 workers missing at multiple energy projects in the Himalayas, including many foreign national workers.

In total, more than 5,000 people are missing in Nepal following last week’s catastrophic floods, which were triggered by a glacier collapse .

The death toll has risen to nearly 1,300 people in Nepal and 21 in China, according to authorities in each country.

CNN’s Hanako Montgomery, Ross Adkin, Bhadra Sharma, Hilary Whiteman, Kosh Koirala and Satish Cheney contributed to this post.

CNN has spoken to two relatives of a hydropower plant worker found by crews in northern Nepal on Friday – both of whom first caught wind of the rescue after seeing the man’s photo circulating online.

Sanjay Sah, a 30-year-old mechanical foreman from the eastern Saptari district, emerged from the cavernous, muddy tunnel in Rasuwa during a mammoth emergency operation along Nepal’s Trishuli River.

His father, Ramphal, said he initially “didn’t believe it.” “When I saw his photo, there was no limit to my happiness,” Ramphal told CNN. “Locals, relatives and well-wishers came to my home to express happiness.”

Ramphal is now waiting at Biratnagar Airport, southeastern Nepal, to travel to Kathmandu and reunite with his son, who he is receiving medical treatment alongside the other survivor, Kabir Maharjan, 45, at a military hospital in the capital.

Signs of life from the labyrinthine tunnel network were thought to be rare after catastrophic floods, triggered by a glacier collapse , hit the region last week. Almost 1,300 people have died in Nepal, with thousands still missing, including about 900 workers at various hydropower projects that run along the Trishuli River.

Sah’s sister, Sudha, told CNN she was “hopeful for his survival,” having tracked news of the rescue online. “I saw his photo,” the 19-year-old woman said. “I was really surprised.”

China on Thursday announced the relocation of its customs facilities at a port in Tibet along its border with Nepal over concerns about potential disaster risks.

Zhangmu Port, about 40 miles away from flood-hit Gyirong, will adjust the location of its customs and immigration inspection facilities from September 5.

The move is to “safeguard the personal and property safety of inbound and outbound travelers,” authorities said, adding that “the risk of geological disasters is prominent.”

China has not updated its number of deaths and missing from the disaster since Wednesday, when it reported that 21 were killed and over 500 missing.

China has received over 800 phone inquiries from family members of the missing, according to state media Xinhua.

The brother of a man missing for more than nine days after devastating flash floods in Nepal rendered him trapped in a tunnel near the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Project has said the recovery of two workers renewed the family’s hope his brother might return alive.

“We hope the rest of the team are all inside together, that they have somehow helped each other to stay alive,” Kshitiz Samaser Regmi, 30, told CNN via telephone.

Regmi explained that his brother, 40-year-old Niraj Babu Regmi whose wife and two daughters are waiting for him at their home in Abu Khaireni, usually works at a different site, but had been moved to Trishuli just two days before the flood hit.

“We don’t know if he was inside, whether he is dead or alive. But we are seeing the team’s working day and night and this helps and brings us hope,” he said.

Two days after the flood destroyed swathes of infrastructure on the Nepal-China border, Regmi went with his father and brother to try to reach the tunnel, but were held back by debris-strewn floors, broken bridges and roads.

The ground was difficult to walk on, he said, and his family are now relying on the hard work of rescue teams which he said is “keeping our hope alive.”

“If he is brought out, I would immediately go to him, bring him whatever he wants and needs and be there for him during his recovery,” Regmi promised.

CNN is receiving more information on how the rescuers at the Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station are pushing ahead with their mission, with two people pulled from the wreckage so far.

Army rescuers are digging by hand at a specific point at the top of the stricken tunnel to try to reach any survivors inside, geologist Arnold Dix, who’s advising the operation, told CNN.

Dix calls the area the “Goldilocks zone,” where he believes workers could have survived.

Outside the tunnel’s entrance was completely blocked by the landslide. Rescuers found the entrance to the tunnel on Monday morning – five days after the flood – and have been been methodically digging since then.

The discovery of two men alive in Trishuli 3A on Friday has given rescuers “renewed hope” at other power stations where almost 900 workers remain missing, Dix said.

Two people have been rescued from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal, a dramatic breakthrough more than a week after catastrophic floods hit the country’s border with China.

Today’s miraculous rescues are a rare bright spot in what has been a devastating nine days for Nepal and China.

Last Wednesday, just after 8:30 a.m. Nepal time, a large piece of glacier near the countries’ border detached from a mountainside. That glacial collapse triggered a massive landslide and catastrophic flash flooding in both countries.

Entire communities were swept away without warning. Homes, schools, playgrounds, and other markers of life were reduced to a gushing river of “liquid cement.”

Hundreds of people were killed, and thousands more were left missing, many of them foreigners who had visited the Himalayas for a once-in-a-lifetime religious pilgrimage.

In the long nine days since the disaster, authorities have been contending with communication blackouts, road blockages and the threat of further floods, as they try to rescue survivors and recover the bodies of victims.

While thousands of people have been rescued so far, hundreds have been found dead. With morgues at capacity, Nepali authorities were forced to bury hundreds of bodies in a mass grave.

The plight of the nearly 1,000 workers trapped in Nepal’s vast system of hydropower tunnels added a new element of terror and challenge for rescuers, with specialized teams coming in to assist Nepali authorities with the daunting rescue.

Despite a colossal effort, as the days ticked on with no sign of life inside the muddy darkness, hopes had dimmed for recovering the workers alive.

Then, this morning, rescuers heard voices.

We’re hearing from the first man who was rescued today at the hydropower tunnel.

In a video seen online, Sanjay Sah was heard asking what the date was — he had no idea how many days he was trapped inside the facility.

The clip showed him lying under a blanket and wearing an oxygen mask. The 30-year-old mechanical foreman said it took some time to get others in the tunnel to evacuate and that he didn’t have enough time to escape himself.

Sah said usually there would only a handful of people in the area where he was in the tunnel but there were 40 to 45 people present when disaster struck. He did not say why there were more people.

“It was my responsibility to save everyone’s life,” he said.

He said he thinks there might still be some people trapped inside. “I don’t think everyone was able to escape. The tunnel is very long,” he said.

Sah said he kept his spirits up by chanting Hindu mantras while inside the tunnel.

CNN’s Hanako Montgomery witnesses the massive rescue operation underway at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant, where two men were found alive after nine days trapped in a tunnel.

The rescue has renewed hopes more people will be found alive in the tunnel.

Two men were rescued from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal, a dramatic breakthrough more than a week after catastrophic floods hit the country’s border with China. It’s not clear how many people are inside the tunnel, according to a lawmaker. CNN's Hanako Montgomery reports from the scene of the rescue operations.

The two men rescued alive after nine days trapped in a hydropower tunnel in Nepal have arrived at the Birendra Army Hospital in Chhauni, Kathmandu.

Images from a CNN team on the ground showed the men being stretchered from a helicopter to a waiting ambulance.

Sanjay Sah, 30, and Kabir Maharjan, 45, were rescued on Friday morning from the tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant, where rescuers had been working for more than a week in the hopes of finding people alive.

CNN’s Hanako Montgomery and Daniel Campisi are at the hydropower plant where earlier two men were miraculously pulled from a tunnel after being trapped inside for more than a week.

Photos they filed from the scene showed rescuers continuing efforts to locate other workers who are believed to remain trapped in there.

As you can see from the photos coming in, the area is incredibly remote and connectivity is limited, underscoring just how tough this rescue effort remains for those working day and night to save their friends and colleagues.

Amid a surge of hope after two men were pulled alive from a hydro tunnel nine days after the disaster, the walls of buildings outside the Trishuli barracks testify to just how many are still missing.

Posters carrying the names, ages, and nationalities of the missing still plaster the walls. Most are Nepali, while some are Korean and Chinese. And many are pictured wearing high-visibility clothing and hard hats.

More than 5,000 people are missing in Nepal following last week’s catastrophic floods, and more than 900 of those people were workers at hydropower projects.

This time last Friday crowds of people were gathered outside this barracks seeking information about missing loved ones. Today around two dozen people have gathered here.

Images show the rescues of two men from a tunnel at a hydropower plant in Nepal on Friday.

Video released by the Nepali Army showed the moments after rescuers reached the two workers who were freed after nine days trapped underground.

We are beginning to get more information from the Nepal Electricity Authority on the two men who were rescued alive from a flood-stricken hydropower tunnel, nine days after the disaster.

The first man has been identified as 30-year-old Sanjay Sah, a mechanical foreman from Saptari district in eastern Nepal.

The second man is Kabir Maharjan, 45, a mechanical supervisor from Kathmandu.

Both men are being treated at a military hospital in Kathmandu, according to the Nepali Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Sah is in stable condition, while Maharjan is in critical condition and under intensive care, according to the PMO.

We are getting new details about how the rescue of two men from a flood-stricken hydropower tunnel unfolded in Nepal.

“Don’t panic, we are rescuing you,” emergency workers said after they heard voices from the tunnel early Friday, according to Nepali lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane.

Rescuers then heard a response of “Okay,” said Neupane, who has been involved in operations at the site.

The two men were pulled out alive, nine days after being trapped by the devastating floods along the Nepal-China border.

articles.title: Three crucial questions facing Farage at Reform conference
articles.summary: Can the Reform UK leader put his policies into action, and become prime minister?
articles.body:
More than 30 years after he first stood for Parliament, Nigel Farage seems to be approaching the climax of his long, storied, and controversial career.

The big unknown: can the 62-year-old put his radical policies into practice by becoming prime minister?

The latest revelations about the party's apparent attitude to donations have ended up dragging Reform into another cycle of bad headlines.

Arguably how it plays out depends on the answers to three central questions.

Will allegations about cash permanently damage Farage?

The Reform leader is already facing investigations into his own finances and those of his party, and concerns about his friendship with a convicted fraudster.

And now there is the possibility of yet more inquiries after an undercover sting which targeted Reform's handling of wealthy donors.

An investigation, filmed by Verbatim Investigations and broadcast by Channel 4 News, shows a senior Farage aide suggesting a way to get around electoral law to secure a foreign donation of £500,000 for the party.

Reform denies any wrongdoing and claims to have "been the target of a hoax perpetuated by foreign funded climate change activists".

Meanwhile Farage's personal popularity already seems to be slightly on the slide and before news of the investigation broke, I spoke to commentators about the party's prospects.

"Among true believers Nigel Farage's personal ratings remain as strong as ever," says Luke Tryl from pollsters More in Common.

"But among the wider public he's taken a dip from being the party leader with the highest net approval this time last year, to being close to tying [Green Party leader Zack] Polanski at the bottom of the pack today".

The barrage of questions about finances prompted the Reform leader to quit Parliament and call the Clacton by-election but his resounding victory in that contest last month has not quietened his critics.

Even some on Farage's own side believe the stresses of the summer have changed the Reform leader's mood during public appearances.

"Why has Nigel, the most successful politician across 25 years, changed from the man who people want to have a drink with?" asks Tim Montgomerie, the Tory defector who was recently suspended from Reform for criticising senior figures.

"He's looked miserable, defensive, and complaining. He needs to get over it, and I think we'll see a better, more attractive Nigel in the coming days."

Farage's biographer, the veteran political journalist Michael Crick, has also noticed a shift.

"You've seen a much more aggressive Farage in the last three or four months. He's gone from the affable to the laughable," says Crick. "That's not going to appeal to waverers, or to moderate conservatives who might be thinking about defecting."

Crick is one of at least eight journalists to have been banned from Reform's conference. Many of them have uncovered uncomfortable details about the party's finances.

In response, Reform says that they have granted accreditation to at least 1,000 members of the media.

The party's 15 months of consistently leading opinion polls are now over.

That is partly due to a resurgent Labour Party under Andy Burnham, and the rise of Restore, a party led by former Reform MP Rupert Lowe.

But regular headlines about party finances, plus the ongoing parliamentary investigation into Farage's decision not to register the £5m "unconditional gift" he received from a billionaire, could also be changing voters' minds.

"People still think Britain isn't working," says Tryl. "And the populist right is doing well in pretty much every European country. But the £5m gift, Nigel Farage's friendship with Donald Trump, and the [US] president's war in Iran have prompted some concerns about Reform".

The party's strategy is to fight back, talk up the likelihood of a snap election next spring and unveil plans for their first 100 days in government. This includes a relentless onslaught of new policies from housing, to the economy and immigration.

"We are in an attention economy and the moment you stop swimming, you die," says one party strategist. "We need to keep it up."

The appearance at the conference today of France's 30-year-old right-wing star Jordan Bardella, is an attempt to show off the international links Farage has fostered. Bardella could be France's prime minister if his colleague Marine Le Pen wins the presidency

In the coming weeks Reform plan to unveil more members of their "shadow cabinet". Insiders say their new recruits will be experienced, talented figures from outside politics. "You'll be impressed. I promise," says one involved.

Yet Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has also refreshed her top team and is showing signs of successfully rebuilding her party's reputation.

"The big risk for Reform is if the Tories pull ahead consistently," says Tryl. "There is a chunk of Tory-Reform waverers who only care about beating Labour, and they will vote for whoever is in the lead in the polls."

"Burnham is a more formidable opponent," concedes Tim Montgomerie. "But however much charisma and vibe the PM has, reality will soon catch up with him."

"There aren't going to be any singalongs at conference this year," says a Reform aide. "Or any COVID deniers."

At last year's event, regional mayor Andrea Jenkyns sang a self-penned rock song on stage, and a guest speaker claimed that Covid vaccines were linked to the cancers of King Charles III and the Princess of Wales. This time, the party is hoping to project a far more serious image.

Farage has also finally surmounted many of the internal problems that bedevilled his previous parties. Ukip in particular had significant struggles with money, resources and organisation.

In contrast, Reform UK has oodles of cash thanks to the generosity of crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne. The party recently received another £4m from Ben Delo, a crypto billionaire.

The party has in just two years built a slick press, marketing and social media operation.

But insiders say there are still problems with candidate selection and polling, and Farage's loyalty to long-term aides is partly to blame.

"There are too many staff who Nigel's had for too long, who he is loyal to, but who won't take Reform from where they are to where they need to be," says Montgomerie.

"The quality of Reform opinion polling is nowhere near as good as the Tories are getting. They never know what's going on at the ground level. Their intelligence at the last three by-elections has been way off."

The aggressive style of the party's home affairs spokesman, Zia Yusuf, has also led to internal friction.

Yusuf is credited with professionalising the party and is hugely popular with Reform members, but not with all of his colleagues. Last month he called former Tory Defence Secretary Ben Wallace a "traitor to Britain" and was reprimanded by Farage.

"Zia's a valued colleague," says one party insider with a grin. Others are more blunt and believe the current situation is unsustainable. "You can't keep blowing stuff up. You can't keep on massacring your own side," says one senior Farage ally. "Nigel is loyal but he's also pragmatic."

Reform may have had a difficult few months, yet they have maintained a big base of supporters.

"It's easy to think they are finished and on the way out," says Crick.

"But to have more than 20% in the opinion polls is way beyond what they got at the election, and it's a very good base to build from".

Whether or not Burnham calls a snap general election next spring, Farage is in the best position of his life to get hold of real power.

This weekend's conference, and how Farage responds to the latest allegations about his colleagues, should give us a strong sign as to whether he is ruthless and focussed enough to achieve it.

articles.title: Indian farmers struggle to meet the demand for avocados
articles.summary: Demand for avocados is booming in India and local growers hope to grab more of the market.
articles.body:
Fifteen years ago there was almost no market for avocados in India, remembers Sunil Bopaiah.

Ripe fruit would fall off trees and be eaten by dogs, earning avocados the unappetising name dog fruit, he says.

Bopaiah has been working in India's plantation industry for 26 years, he's currently group manager at Cottanad Plantations, which grows cocoa, rubber, coffee, spices and fruits, including avocado, in the hills of Wayanad in the southern Indian state of Kerala.

"We never planted avocado as our main crop. We introduced it as a shade tree for coffee plantations, and only later realised it could become a profitable business," he says.

He says the turning point was around 2011 when Bollywood star Shilpa Shetty said she used avocado for skincare.

"Overnight, prices doubled and then kept rising," he says.

Cottanad has responded to that demand by planting avocado trees on 40 acres. Last year they harvested between 10 and 15 tonnes of fruit. In three of four years time they hope to raise that to 40 to 50 tonnes.

"We completely changed the way we grow avocados after learning from South African experts. Today we use raised beds, wider spacing and different planting methods because avocado roots are highly vulnerable to diseases," Bopaiah says.

There's plenty of scope for Indian farmers to step-up production.

"When we studied the market, we found a huge gap between demand and supply. India imports around 15,000 tonnes of avocados every year, while domestic production is only about 8,000–9,000 tonnes," says Manilal Palliyath who helps promote India's avocado industry.

He sees a big opportunity for farmers, particularly as traditional crops have suffered.

"Coffee and pepper have suffered because of changing climatic conditions, making diversification essential for farmers."

While demand is growing in India, it's not always for locally grown fruit.

"Indian-grown avocados are improving and there are some great farmers working with local varieties, but the quality and availability can vary significantly depending on the season and region," says Hussain Shahzad, the executive chef at Hunger Inc. Hospitality.

The group owns four restaurants in Mumbai, including Veronica's and The Bombay Canteen.

"We have explored different varieties of avocados available in India, but the imported ones currently offer the consistency we need in terms of flavour, texture, size, and ripening," he says

But like many in the catering industry, he would like to source ingredients locally.

"We are always interested in exploring better local produce as it evolves. Supporting Indian agriculture and working with indigenous ingredients is central to how we approach food."

Matching the quality and consistency of imported fruit is the goal of some Indian entrepreneurs.

Harshit Godha is the founder of Indo-Israel Avocado Nursery in Bhopal, in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.

He founded the nursery business in 2021, after spending a month in Israel learning about the industry.

Since then, business has been brisk. Over the last five years Godha has supplied around 18,000 avocado plants to farmers across India.

All of the saplings are international varieties like Hass and Pinkerton.

"Israel grows avocados on approximately 13,000 hectares - a small country with almost no rainfall for eight months of the year. This is precisely why Israeli avocado technology is the most advanced in the world," Godha says.

Getting a commercial orchard up and running is not easy. It is a very different operation from the traditional way of cultivating avocados in India, where they were planted among other crops for shade.

For a start, you can't just grow a tree from seed. A commercial tree comprises a rootstock, chosen for its tolerance to local conditions, grafted to the upper half which determines what sort of fruit is produced.

Once that's done the trees need a lot of attention.

"When you put in a professional orchard, you have to know the techniques of pruning. A tree can grow up to 25 feet within six to seven years, and harvesting at 25 feet is next to impossible," Godha says.

"Aggressive" pruning is needed to keep the harvest at a height that's convenient for workers.

On top of that an avocado tree cannot easily pollinate itself. To get fruit two different varieties of avocado trees have to be planted right next to each other. One variety needs to be open as a female at the exact same time the other variety is releasing pollen as a male."

"If a farmer gets this planting ratio wrong, the trees will fail to produce fruit, no matter how advanced the irrigation tech is. This single botanical detail is what separates a highly profitable, high-yielding orchard from one that looks great on paper but fails in reality," says Godha.

Using popular foreign varieties is one way of modernising India's avocado industry. Another is improving trees that have in India for generations.

"The biggest issue with the avocado trees in India are that every backyard tree is genetically different," says Dr Ganeshan Karunakaran, the principal scientist at the ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru.

"That is why Indian markets are flooded with mixed fruit of varying quality. Standard varieties are essential if we want a reliable commercial market."

For 25 years he has been working on a breeding project which has released two varieties, based on local trees.

"Our objective is to provide farmers with uniform, high-yielding, good-quality planting material rather than thousands of different unnamed trees," Karunakaran says.

He is also concerned about unregulated nurseries selling unidentified, or diseased plants.

"Farmers may unknowingly buy diseased plants. The trees may look healthy initially, but after five or seven years they can suddenly die, causing huge financial losses," he says.

Despite the challenges, farmers see the potential in switching to avocado cultivation.

Shiju Sebastian was an early adopter. Eight years ago he dedicated two acres of his farm in Wayanad Kerala, to the crop.

"Farmers are willing to grow avocados, but they need proper guidance and assured markets," he says.

This year he's harvesting 3,500kg of the fruit, all of which is sold in the city of Bengalaru.

"Avocado will never fail you. It's such a loving and lovable fruit. I have fallen in love with this fruit now. I'm planning to plant another three acres — only avocado."
